chunks: AC coupling capacitors. The question: What is an AC coupling capacitor?
An AC coupling capacitor sits in series with a signal. It passes the changing part and blocks the steady DC part.
That lets you connect two circuits that sit at different DC levels without upsetting either one's bias.
Together with the resistance after it, the capacitor forms a high-pass filter. So it also drops very slow signals.
Imagine two floating decks at different heights. A flexible link between them carries every bounce and wobble across, but it does not force one deck up to the other's height.
The wobble gets through and the height difference stays put. The link is not perfect. Very slow motions pass poorly, just as very low frequencies are weakened.
The source can sit at any DC level; the capacitor blocks it. The divider R1/R2 holds the far node at V DD/2 and also forms the resistance that the capacitor charges through.
Seen from the capacitor, R1 and R2 are in parallel (5 kilohms).
AC coupling: passing the changing part of a signal while blocking DC. DC bias: the steady voltage a circuit input sits at so it can work properly.
High-pass filter: a filter that passes high frequencies and drops low ones. Corner frequency: where the signal is down 3 decibels, at f c equals 1 over (2 pi RC) .
Time constant: tau equals RC , which sets how long the circuit takes to settle at startup.
You AC-couple a signal into an input that has a 10 kilohms bias network, using a 1 microfarads capacitor.
The corner is 1 over (2 pi times 10 000 times 10 to the -6) , about 16 hertz. A 1 kilohertz tone passes almost unchanged.
The DC level is blocked, and the input keeps its own bias. A 16 hertz tone is down 3 decibels. That is the whole idea.
"An AC coupling capacitor in series blocks DC and passes AC, so two stages with different DC bias levels can connect.
Together with the input resistance after it, it forms a high-pass filter with corner one over two pi R C, so I choose C so that corner is well below the lowest signal frequency.
The cost is a startup settling time of a few R C, and I need a bias network after the cap to set the DC level."
